sentences.text: Only one species, Ludiortyx hoffmanni, is currently accepted for this genus.
Fossils of Ludiortyx were found in the Montmartre Formation near Paris, France.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Ludiortyx within the family Rallidae.
Ludiortyx lived during the Late Eocene, between 56 and 33.9 million years ago, spanning the Ypresian to Priabonian stages.
The evolutionary relationships of Ludiortyx are debated, with some researchers suggesting it is an ancestral rail while others place it in the prehistoric landfowl group Quercymegapodiidae.
